stem: Meera notices that the marigold plants grown from seeds in her school garden look very similar to the parent plant, but a few of them have slightly different flower colours. Which statement best explains how reproduction produces both this similarity and this variation?

options.text: Reproduction passes inherited instructions from parent to offspring, giving resemblance, while small changes in these instructions create variation.
Reproduction only makes exact copies, so variation must come from a completely separate process.
Reproduction creates variation first, and this variation then produces the inherited instructions.
Reproduction keeps the species alive, so the instructions passed to offspring do not matter.

teacher.key_rationale: Continuity comes from inherited instructions passed from parent to offspring (resemblance), and small changes in those instructions produce variation, matching the chapter relationship reproduction and inherited instructions -> continuity plus variation -> persistence of life. B denies variation arises within reproduction; C reverses the relationship; D omits the role of inherited instructions.
